root_idea.summary: The root centers on letting something flow out or be poured forth, especially a liquid.
root_idea.development: The literal branch concerns pouring or spilling water, blood, and tears. The sexual noun السِّفاح develops through the image of water being poured wastefully outside marriage. Maqāyīs treats the mountain-foot noun سَفْح as an ibdāl branch from صَفْح and the maysir-arrow term سَفِيح as anomalous to the central principle.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The masculine and feminine Quranic forms are inflections of the same active-participial lexeme مُسَافِحٌ.

senses.definition: A fornicator; one who engages in sexual intercourse outside marriage.
senses.usage_conditions: Active participle of Form III. The feminine form مُسَافِحَةٌ denotes a female fornicator; the Quranic occurrences use masculine and feminine inflections in marital and sexual-ethics contexts.

senses.definition: Poured forth or shed; in the Quranic usage, blood that has been poured out.
senses.usage_conditions: Passive participle of Form I. The Quranic construction describes blood as poured forth, presenting it as the result of pouring or shedding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour out water, or to shed blood and tears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Transitive Form I usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour or flow out intransitively, especially of water or tears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive Form I usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Stretched or extended upon the ground, said of a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of a camel’s posture or placement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To do a deed that brings no profit; hence, one who does such a deed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II usage and its related participial description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To shed blood mutually; by extension, to fight or engage in camel-hocking with one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form III or Form VI construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make horses run without a wager.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form IV usage associated with the maysir arrow called السَّفِيح.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become poured out or forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as an attributed usage without a named authority in the cited entry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The base, foot, lower part, or spreading face of a mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun may refer to the lower or ground-resting part of the mountain; plural سُفُوحٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Soft or smooth, slippery rocks.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Plural lexical usage distinct from the mountain-base sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Shedding abundantly, especially tears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited usage describes an eyelid that sheds copious tears.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sack; in the dual, a pair of sacks placed on a camel like panniers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal object term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thick or coarse garment or cloak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal usage distinct from the sack sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A maysir arrow to which no portion, penalty, or winning share is assigned.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: One of the unnotched arrows used in the game of maysir.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A great shedder of blood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive agent noun; السَّفَّاحُ is also recorded as the name of a sword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper-name usage derived from the intensive bloodshed sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A great giver; one who gives much.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported figurative extension, including the giving of many gifts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fluent or eloquent in speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported figurative usage; the cited discussion also records an interpretation glossed as chaste.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pouring out or forth, applied to water, blood, or tears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Active participial adjective of the literal pouring branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bald in the fore part of the head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized physical description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where water is poured or flows out, or where blood or tears are shed; an outlet or discharge-place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Plural مَسَافِحُ; a valley may have several such outlets.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Broad, thick, coarse, or large in bodily build or in a body part.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in descriptions of breadth in the armpits or ribs and of a long, thick neck; the cited examples do not establish a narrower object-class restriction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of a horse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper-name usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression ابن مُسَافِحَةٍ, a son born of fornication; by extension, offspring of fornication.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional kinship expression, distinct from the meaning ‘fornicatress’ of مُسَافِحَةٌ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pouring and shedding liquid are represented in the Quranic passive sense and the Classical Form I entry.
Intransitive flowing of water or tears.
Making horses run without a wager.
Intensive bloodshed sense and derived sword name.
Participial form for one doing an unprofitable deed.
Broad bodily build or body part.
Thick, coarse, or large bodily description.
Fornicator/fornicatress sense and the offspring-of-fornication expression.

cautions: The mountain-slope noun سَفْحٌ is treated by Maqāyīs as an ibdāl branch from صَفْح, although it is recorded in the supplied Lane entry under سفح.
The maysir-arrow term سَفِيحٌ is explicitly treated by Maqāyīs as anomalous to the central pouring sense.
The Form V meaning ‘to be or become poured out’ is reported in Lane without a named authority.
